value.name: rosa explains the codicil
value.description: Rosa tells Daniel that the codicil was not a punishment but a deliberate recognition of the family's situation and his separate life.
evidence: "I will say it again," Rosa said, "because I want you to hear it the second time. She saw through it. And it did not matter. She loved you, Daniel. She loved you the way she loved you, which was not the way you wanted to be loved, and she knew it was not the way you wanted to be loved, and she could not change the way she loved you any more than you could change the way you wanted to be loved, and she made her peace with that long before she got sick. The codicil was not a punishment. It was not even a correction. It was, as far as I could tell from the conversations I had with her in the kitchen on the afternoons when she was telling me what she was thinking — and she did tell me, Daniel, she told me because there was no one else in the house to tell — it was a recognition. She recognized that the house had become a place she lived in with me and that Lucia visited often, and she recognized that you had built a life elsewhere, and she recognized that leaving the house to you would force you to either sell it, which would cost you something, or keep it, which would cost you more, and she decided that what she wanted to leave you was the freedom from that decision. She thought she was being kind to you."

value.name: rosa recalls private conversations
value.description: Rosa reveals that she had repeated kitchen conversations with the woman about her thoughts because there was no one else in the house to tell.
evidence: "...from the conversations I had with her in the kitchen on the afternoons when she was telling me what she was thinking — and she did tell me, Daniel, she told me because there was no one else in the house to tell..."

value.name: woman recognizes household reality
value.description: Rosa says the woman understood that Rosa and Lucia effectively lived in the house while Daniel had built a life elsewhere.
evidence: "She recognized that the house had become a place she lived in with me and that Lucia visited often, and she recognized that you had built a life elsewhere..."

value.name: woman leaves house decision unresolved
value.description: Rosa explains that the woman chose not to leave Daniel the house in order to spare him the burden of deciding whether to sell or keep it.
evidence: "...and she recognized that leaving the house to you would force you to either sell it, which would cost you something, or keep it, which would cost you more, and she decided that what she wanted to leave you was the freedom from that decision."

value.name: rosa frames the codicil as kindness
value.description: Rosa concludes that the woman believed she was acting kindly toward Daniel by making the codicil that way.
evidence: "She thought she was being kind to you."

value.name: daniel cries silently
value.description: Daniel breaks down and cries without making a sound, revealing deep emotional pain.

value.name: rosa recalls earlier silent crying
value.description: Rosa recognizes Daniel's silent crying as something she saw once before when he was eleven and missed making a team.
evidence: which was a way of crying Rosa had seen him do once before, when he was eleven and had failed to make a team he had wanted to make, and which she had not seen him do since.

value.name: daniel rejects rosa's interpretation
value.description: After a pause, Daniel responds that Rosa is wrong about the meaning of the codicil.
evidence: "She was wrong," he said, "after a while."
